record.original_question: Let M be a sigma-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and let Diff_c(M)_{p,0} be the subgroup of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms fixing p whose tangent map at p has positive determinant. Is every formal diffeomorphism of R^n whose linear part has positive determinant realized as the Taylor series at p of some element of Diff_c(M)_{p,0}? Equivalently, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^infinity: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G^n_f(R)_0 surjective?

evidence.quote: Moreover, we prove a result by the author announced in [21], which answers a question posed in an earlier, unpublished version of the survey.

Borel's Theorem for Diffeomorphisms. Let a finite-dimensional smooth manifold M of dimension n be given, p ∈ M and φ be a local chart around p such that φ(p) = 0. For each γ ∈ Diffc(M), let T∞_p(γ) denote the Taylor series of φ ◦ γ ◦ φ−1 around 0. Then T∞_p : Diffc(M)p,0 → Gfn(R)0 is a surjective homomorphism of Lie groups.
In this case, the surjectivity of T∞_p : Diffc(Rn)p,0 → Gfn(R)0 has been established in Lemma 4.2. The Chain Rule for Taylor Polynomials entails that T∞_p is a homomorphism of groups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a $\sigma$-compact smooth manifold of dimension $n>0$, and fix a point $p\in M$. Let $\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)$ denote the group of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms of $M$, and let $\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}$ be the subgroup consisting of those $\gamma\in\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)$ with $\gamma(p)=p$ such that the tangent map $T_p\gamma:T_pM\to T_pM$ has positive determinant. Choose a local chart $\varphi$ around $p$ with $\varphi(p)=0$, and for $\gamma\in\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}$ let $T_p^\infty(\gamma)$ denote the formal Taylor series at $0$ of $\varphi\circ\gamma\circ\varphi^{-1}$. Let $G^n_f(\mathbb{R})_0$ denote the group, under formal composition, of formal power series diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing $0$ whose linear part has positive determinant.

Prove or disprove: the Taylor-series map
$$T_p^\infty:\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}\longrightarrow G^n_f(\mathbb{R})_0$$
is a surjective group homomorphism; equivalently, every formal diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing $0$ with positive-determinant linear part arises as the Taylor expansion at $p$ (in the chart $\varphi$) of some compactly supported smooth diffeomorphism of $M$ in $\mathrm{Diff}_c(M)_{p,0}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is established as a theorem ("Borel's Theorem for Diffeomorphisms"): the Taylor-series map is a surjective homomorphism of Lie groups, with the $\mathbb{R}^n$ case proved via an explicit lemma and the general manifold case reduced to it. This resolves the question affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Borel-type realization for diffeomorphisms (arXiv:0801.1919)
status_evidence.snippet: Borel's Theorem for Diffeomorphisms... T∞_p : Diffc(M)_{p,0} → G^n_f(R)_0 is a surjective homomorphism of Lie groups.
status_evidence.claim: The surjectivity of the Taylor-series homomorphism is proved, resolving the question affirmatively.
